title: Engineering and Integrity Learnings: Gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: Engineering, asset integrity, instrumentation, electrical and management-of-change functions, and the technical authority
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Derived from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; learnings are evidence-linked but should be validated by the organisation before adoption. Draft learnings: the investigation status is in progress.

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate every item before adoption.

bottom_line.text: The release came from a seal fitted with no specification and returned to service without a test to design pressure; neither condition had an engineering owner.
The management-of-change procedure existed but was not used, so the substitution had no review.
Detection only informed and the isolation valves were local-only: the design left the response to people who could not reach the valves.
The probable ignition source was a flameproof lamp with missing bolts, under breakdown-led electrical maintenance.
Integrity warnings and drawings were recorded but not acted on or approved; the records themselves need owners.

items.lesson: If the specification for a pressure-boundary part is lost and no function owns re-establishing it, a substitute part becomes normal practice.
items.explanation: The 1986 meter was built for a rectangular-slot gasket. Its original specification was not on file, and no material specification or procurement policy existed for these gaskets, so locally bought O-rings were fitted as regular practice. The condition persisted because no function owned the specification or the approval of a substitute.

items.barrier: Pressure-boundary integrity: the correct seal to a written specification
items.failure_mode: No specification on file and no approved substitute, so a non-specified O-ring was fitted as regular practice.
items.fix: Re-establish the seal specification and stock only certified parts against it.
items.indicator: % of critical pressure-boundary spares with a specification on file

items.change: Route: technical query. Re-establish the seal design for the meter flange from the maker's data or an engineered equivalent, and quarantine non-conforming seals.
items.indicator: % of critical pressure-boundary spares with a specification and certificate on file

items.lesson: If no standard defines the test for a high-pressure joint before return to service, the quickest available check becomes the test, and a weak joint passes.
items.explanation: After the gasket change on 18 Sep 2020 the system was only pressurised to operating pressure; no hydro test to design pressure was done, and there was no procedure for calibration or return to service of these high-pressure meters. The metering-skid workspace had no specifications, procedures or checklists.

items.failure_mode: No procedure required a test to design pressure, so pressurising to operating pressure was taken as proof of the joint.
items.fix: A return-to-service standard that sets the test, the test pressure and the witness, enforced in the work-order system.
items.indicator: % of pressure-boundary jobs closed with a recorded test result and witness

lint_ok.reason: A pressure test is a procedural barrier by nature; its tier is stated honestly, and the engineering enforcement is the recommendation beside it.

items.change: Route: MOC. Configure the work-order system so a pressure-boundary job cannot be closed, or the equipment released, until a test result against the technical authority's return-to-service standard is entered.
items.indicator: Attempted closures blocked for missing test data, trending to zero

items.lesson: A management-of-change procedure that is published but never triggered lets changes in parts and materials through without review.
items.explanation: The procedure was published in August 2016, but no change had been taken through it since 2018. The switch from the maker's gasket to locally bought O-rings had no change review, and people did not recognise a like-for-unlike replacement as a change.

items.failure_mode: The procedure existed on paper but was not used; the substitution had no risk review.
items.fix: A trigger in the stores and work-order systems that asks for a change reference for any substitute part.
items.indicator: Change reviews raised per month; a long run of zero is a warning

lint_ok.reason: Change review is a management-system barrier; its tier is stated honestly, and the engineering trigger is the recommendation beside it.

items.change: Route: MOC. Build a change-review trigger into the work-order and stores issue screens, so a non-catalogue or substitute part needs a change reference before it is issued.
items.indicator: % of substitute-part issues with a change reference

items.lesson: If fire and gas detection is designed to inform rather than act, every protective action waits on people noticing, checking and deciding.
items.explanation: The hydrocarbon and H2S detectors were configured to the annunciator panel only, with no history in the control system and no automatic shutdown or suppression. No policy required the interlock, and the system was never upgraded, so the first alarm came after people had already seen the cloud.

items.barrier: Fire and gas detection with automatic executive action
items.failure_mode: Detection lit an annunciator only: no shutdown, isolation or suppression, and no signal history.
items.fix: Confirmed-gas logic that starts isolation, and deluge where designed, with every detector signal kept in history.
items.indicator: % of major-release areas covered by automatic executive action

items.change: Route: MOC. Implement confirmed-gas logic that starts isolation by itself (and deluge where designed) in the metering and gas terminal areas, and keep every detector signal in history.
items.barrier: Fire and gas detection with automatic executive action
items.indicator: % of detectors with signal history; proof-test and spurious-trip records reviewed each quarter

items.lesson: Emergency isolation valves that can only be worked at the valve are out of reach in the event they exist for.
items.explanation: The gas terminal emergency valves were supplied as local-manual valves with no remote operation from the control room, and were never upgraded. The vapour cloud kept people away, and the first valve was closed by hand once the shift in-charge reached it.

items.barrier: Emergency isolation of the gas terminal inventory
items.failure_mode: Isolation needed a person at the valve, inside the area the release made unreachable.
items.fix: Remote-operated emergency isolation, worked from the control room and a safe secondary location.
items.indicator: % of identified emergency isolation points with remote operation

items.change: Route: MOC. Convert the gas terminal emergency isolation valves to remotely operated emergency shutdown valves, worked from the control room and a safe secondary location.
items.barrier: Emergency isolation of the gas terminal inventory
items.indicator: % of identified emergency isolation points with remote operation; valve proof-test pass rate

items.lesson: If electrical maintenance in hazardous areas answers breakdowns instead of inspecting explosion protection, defects that do not stop the equipment working stay in service.
items.explanation: A flameproof lamp at the skid had three bolts missing and its glass case open; the committee named it the probable ignition source. Electrical maintenance leaned towards breakdown work with little systematic inspection, and the post-incident audit grouped all nine lamps under one status. The ignition source is probable, not proven.

items.barrier: Ignition control: flameproof integrity of lighting in the hazardous area
items.failure_mode: A flameproof fitting with missing bolts and an open case stayed in service without inspection.
items.fix: Certified replacement fittings, and an inspection programme for explosion-protected equipment with records for each item.
items.indicator: % of zoned-area fittings with an item-level inspection record in the current cycle

items.change: Route: MOC. Replace the old high-pressure mercury vapour flameproof lamps in zoned areas with certified fittings with a lower surface temperature.
items.barrier: Ignition control: flameproof integrity of lighting
items.indicator: % of zoned-area luminaires replaced with certified fittings

items.lesson: If inspection results are recorded but nobody owns turning them into a decision, the organisation knows about degradation and keeps operating with it.
items.explanation: Wall loss found in 2017 had no corrective plan three years later; pitting found in July 2019 on a zero-corrosion-allowance 36-inch line was treated by painting, with no fitness-for-service review; the four-year thickness schedule slipped. These lines did not cause this release: the learning is about how integrity warnings are handled.

items.failure_mode: Measurements were taken but not turned into corrective plans or fitness-for-service decisions, and the inspection schedule slipped.
items.fix: A fitness-for-service decision for every wall-loss finding, tracked to closure, with inspection due dates that escalate when overdue.
items.indicator: Open wall-loss findings without a fitness-for-service decision

items.change: Route: technical query. Carry out fitness-for-service assessments on the 2017 and July 2019 wall-loss locations, and repair, re-rate or replace as the technical authority decides.
items.indicator: Open wall-loss findings without a fitness-for-service decision, reviewed monthly

items.lesson: If drawings drift from the field and vendor drawings are not approved, maintenance and emergency isolation are planned from a picture that is wrong.
items.explanation: The original metering drawings were lost; a vendor prepared replacements that were not checked or approved, and the valve and meter configuration on them did not match the field. No function owned keeping the as-built record true.

items.failure_mode: An unapproved vendor drawing that did not match the field was the only drawing in use.
items.fix: Field-verified, approved drawings for safety-critical systems, with approval required for every vendor drawing.
items.indicator: % of safety-critical drawings field-verified and approved

lint_ok.reason: Drawing control is a records barrier; no stronger tier applies to keeping a drawing true to the field.

items.change: Route: engineering standard revision. Require operator checking and approval of every vendor drawing before it is controlled, and field-verify and re-issue the gas terminal drawings, starting with metering and emergency isolation.
items.why_not_stronger: Drawing control is a records process; no engineering control replaces checking a drawing against the field.

lint_ok.reason: The document-control standard is the system fix for this L3/L4 records gap; no stronger tier applies.

items.indicator: % of safety-critical drawings field-verified and approved; vendor drawings in use without approval

sections.heading: Engineering decisions pending
sections.intro: Options only: the technical authority settles these. No engineering value is set here beyond what the cited records state.

items.decision: What test, and what test pressure, must a joint on these high-pressure meters pass after pressure-boundary work before it returns to service?
options: A hydro test to design pressure
Another test method the technical authority approves
A change to the joint design that allows a different test
items.trade_offs: The cited records show only that operating pressure was used and a hydro test to design pressure was not; the test values are for the technical authority to set.

items.decision: How is the seal for the 1986 meter flange to be specified, and is a substitute acceptable?
options: Replace the meter with one that can be kept to specification
items.trade_offs: Recovering the maker's data may not be possible for equipment of this age; replacement removes the problem but takes longer.

items.decision: Is the pitted zero-corrosion-allowance section of the 36-inch line fit for service after painting?
items.trade_offs: The record gives the measured loss and the design thickness with zero corrosion allowance, and asks whether painting suffices; it gives no fitness-for-service result.

items.decision: Which executive actions should confirmed gas detection start in the metering and gas terminal areas, and on what voting logic?
options: Alarm with remote manual isolation from the control room
items.trade_offs: Automatic action shortens the response but needs voting logic to limit spurious trips.

items.decision: Which emergency isolation valves become remotely operated, and from where?
options: From the control room and a safe secondary location
Automatically on confirmed gas, with remote override
items.trade_offs: The records show the valves were local-only and unreachable; the choice of location depends on where a release could deny access.

items.decision: How is the thickness inspection schedule restored, and what serves as the baseline where the original data is lost?
options: Use the first surviving measurements as the baseline
items.trade_offs: Most pipes have only two measurements on file, which limits any corrosion-rate estimate.

items.when: before a pressure-boundary part is bought or issued
items.text: A specification reference for the part is on file, with any approved substitute recorded.

items.when: at return to service after pressure-boundary work
items.text: The test record shows the test, the test pressure, the result and the witness.

items.when: during and after calibration of a critical meter
items.text: Every setting change, including one reversed, is recorded with as-found and as-left values on a checklist.

items.when: before a drawing is used to plan work or an isolation
items.text: The drawing is approved and matches the field configuration.
Every fire and gas detector signal is kept in history in the control system.
Every pressure transmitter shown on the drawing delivers live, retained data, and control-system clocks agree.
The baseline and each measurement are recorded, with the corrective decision for every loss found.

items.when: at each inspection of hazardous-area electrical equipment
items.text: Each fitting has its own record of condition, not one status for a group.

limits: The barriers here are written in this pack because barrier-learnings has not been run for this sample; barrier-learnings is the next step, and should become their source.
The ignition source is probable, not proven, and the wall-loss lines did not cause this release.
